# pruebapaquete

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/joaquin0307/pruebapaquete/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/joaquin0307/pruebapaquete/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![test-coverage](https://github.com/joaquin0307/pruebapaquete/actions/workflows/test-coverage.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/joaquin0307/pruebapaquete/actions/workflows/test-coverage.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

The goal of pruebapaquete is to:
distintos tipos de sumas. con numeros positivos y negativos.


## Installation

You can install the development version of pruebapaquete from [GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("joaquin0307/pruebapaquete")
```

## Example

This is a basic example which shows you how to solve a common problem:

```{r example}
library(pruebapaquete)
## basic example code
mi_funcion(8,9)
mi_funcion(10,9)
```

What is special about using `README.Rmd` instead of just `README.md`? You can include R chunks like so:

```{r cars}
mi_funcion(3,8)
```

You'll still need to render `README.Rmd` regularly, to keep `README.md` up-to-date. `devtools::build_readme()` is handy for this.


In that case, don't forget to commit and push the resulting figure files, so they display on GitHub and CRAN.
